summary: The post tools take a --film v1|v2 flag (default v1, whose behaviour is proven unchanged). docs/shots_v2.json drives v2: 960 frames, 32.0 s, cut pairs 240|241, 420|421, 600|601, 780|781, all derived from the table. assemble.py writes out/v2/ (preview: out/v2/preview/), make_overlays.py writes renders/overlays_v2 (S01-S03 exactly v1; S04 pill 616 -> out by 776 with the live zoom chip from renders/meta/s04_subject.json; nothing in the finale). render_finals.py --film v2 runs stage A (tile scenes + s04_subject + the overscan still), stage B (make_hex_tiles --require-final) and stage C (s05_finale). qa_finals.py --film v2 adds s04-subject-hold, s04-overscan, seam, title-unchanged and tiles-final. The README has a v2 section in Chinese. No GPU used.

design.shots_v2_json: Still a JSON list with every v1 field, so v1-style loaders work. S01-S03 are copied verbatim from docs/shots.json plus "source": "v1" and a v2_note. s04_subject (601-780, 192 spp, threshold 0.01) and s05_finale (781-960, 384 spp, threshold 0.02) carry "source": "new", cost_cap_gpu_hours (0.45 / 0.7), estimates (8 / 13 s per frame). s04_subject adds static_hold [150,180] and an overscan block (switch, frame 180, 2544x2204 / 1272x1102, crop offset 312,562, output path). s05_finale adds tile_scenes (the twelve t_* ids), hex_tiles (script, --require-final, manifest, 180 f, 1152x998), match_cut_from (s04_subject f180 -> f1) and title_same_as (s05_title f61-120 = v2 f121-180). The tools read these fields instead of hard-coding them.
design.assemble: FILMS table: v1 = docs/shots.json, renders/film|film_comp|film_comp_clean|overlays, out/ (and out/preview/), 900 frames. v2 = docs/shots_v2.json, renders/film_v2|film_comp_v2|film_comp_clean_v2|overlays_v2, out/v2/ (and out/v2/preview/), names LaRenderer_opening_v2[_clean][_master].mp4/.mov, 960 frames. Cut pairs are derived from the table for both films; for v1 they equal the old constant. In v2 overview_1fps.png is always made, with the recipe that made out/overview_1fps.png (scripts/contact_sheet.py, 320 px tiles of captioned film frames 15, 45, ...); that recipe reproduces the v1 file byte-for-byte. v2 uses 8 columns so its 32 tiles fill a 2560x720 grid exactly. v1 makes the overview only with --overview. New v2 film QA: finale_overlay_free (no overlay alpha on 781-960). With --slug the v2 caption QA ignores the slug's lower-right zone (x>=1400, y>=940). A v2 run refuses to write any v1 folder. --dry-run prints the plan. The v1 manifest keeps exactly its original keys; v2 adds film, table, seconds, cut_pairs, placeholders_by_shot and intermediates.
design.overlays: configure(film) rebinds the timeline before the Overlay is built (fork workers inherit it). v2: PILLS[:4] and the S01/S03 chips are the v1 objects; S04 is pill 'High-res textures' (lemon) 616 -> window end 776 (pop-out reaches scale 0 on 776), chip 631 -> 776 reading per-frame zoom from renders/meta/s04_subject.json. There is no texel chip. Self-test asserts: S01-S03 windows equal v1, S04 window 616/776, frames 777-960 empty, table 781-960/960, and the fallback checkpoints. The meta now exists: the chip reads x1.0 (f631) -> x2.3 (f680) -> x6.3 (f720) -> x7.4 (f736, the push's SETTLE peak) -> x7.0 (f749-775). If the meta or its zoom column is missing, the documented fallback zoom = 7.0 ** ease_in_out_sine((local f - 31)/(145 - 31)) is used and logged. Refuses to write v2 overlays into renders/overlays.
design.render_finals: v2 runs in stages. Stage A is one queue across both GPUs, longest jobs first. It holds the twelve tile scenes (frames 1..loop from renders/meta/t_<name>.json, 180 if not looped; chunks of 90 frames, so a 60/90 loop is one process), s04_subject f1-180 (chunks of 60, so 3 processes and only 3 loads of the 20K texture) and one overscan job (`--frames 180 --overscan`). Stage B runs tools/venv/bin/python -I scripts/make_hex_tiles.py --require-final (in preview mode without the flag); a non-zero exit blocks stage C and is logged to logs/finals_v2/hex_tiles.log. Stage C is s05_finale f1-180 (chunks of 45, at least one job per GPU). S01-S03 are v1 finals and get no jobs; their completeness is printed. A tile scene with a script but no meta gets a `--no-render` build to write its meta, then its frames are planned. Missing scripts are skipped with a note. Every job is checked afterwards: each expected PNG must exist and end in IEND. The overscan must be 2544x2204 (1272x1102 in preview), and f_0180.png's size and mtime must not change. Estimates use a measured s/f from the shot's meta when present (keys matching s_per_f / spf / sec_per_frame); otherwise the table value or the 0.12 GPU-h tile cap. --frames subsets are clamped to each shot (a subset outside a 60-frame loop plans nothing). Logs and summary go to logs/finals_v2/. ALLOWED {6,7} guard unchanged.
design.overscan_interface: Verified against shots/s04_subject.py, now written: it strips --overscan (or S04_OVERSCAN=1) from argv before D.parse_args, renders frame 180 only (it accepts --frames 180 silently), writes through renders/<mode>/s04_subject/_overscan_tmp/ and os.replace()s to overscan.png, and never rewrites f_0180.png or the meta. render_finals reads the script for the switch: present = --overscan; script missing = the documented expected interface; script without the switch = job not scheduled.
design.qa_finals: v1 path is the original code moved verbatim into main_v1 (only argument parsing moved). v2 runs the v1 frame checks for every v2 shot: completeness, 1920x1080 16-bit shape, finite values, single-frame luma spikes, and final vs preview blocks in final mode. Status per shot is PASS / REVIEW (spikes or flagged blocks) / FAIL (bad shape or non-finite) / incomplete / missing. Then the v1 presets s01-loop, s02-strip and s03-static via scripts/qa_diff.py, with heat-maps and CSVs redirected to renders/qa/v2/ so the v1 QA artefacts are never rewritten. New presets: s04-subject-hold (f150-180, every consecutive pair mean |d| <= 0.5/255, bit-identical pairs counted); s04-overscan (centred crop of overscan.png vs f180, sigma-1 Gaussian blur on both, mean <= 1/255, p99 reported, size checked); seam (s04_subject f180 vs s05_finale f1, sigma-1 blur, mean <= 1/255 and p99 <= 4/255); title-unchanged (s05_finale f121-180 vs v1 s05_title f61-120 in the same mode: mean |d| <= 3/255 for y >= 420 film px on every pair, and each of the 10 letters' left/top/right within +-2 px; letters are found by hue windows of +-12 deg measured on v1 f90, above the floor line y 700); tiles-final (manifest present; preview or placeholder sources count as incomplete, not FAIL; a short tile folder, a missing or wrong-size centre still, or an unknown source is FAIL). Not-yet-rendered inputs are reported as missing, never a crash. Exit 1 only on a FAIL, or on missing/incomplete with --require-complete. The v2 presets follow --shots. Reports go to logs/finals_v2/qa_report.json (final) and qa_report_preview.json.

known_issues: s04_subject's render estimate is ~0.458 GPU-h (table 8 s/f + per-process start-up and 20K texture upload) against the 0.45 cap. render_finals uses a measured s/f automatically once the S04 builder writes one into renders/meta/s04_subject.json (any key matching s_per_f / spf / sec_per_frame). t_jelly_cubes and t_material_balls have null measured s/f, so their estimates use the 0.12 GPU-h cap.

shots/s05_finale.py and six tile scenes (t_disco, t_magnifier, t_desk_lamp, t_lightbulb, t_sunset_bunny, t_toy_town) were not written when I finished. render_finals skips them with a note. Stage C was exercised only with the stub. Re-run --dry-run once they exist.

render_finals (v1 and v2) does not detect stale frames (a script changed after its frames were rendered); delete those frames to re-render. For the overscan it warns when overscan.png is more than 10 min older than f_0180.png, because the seam needs both from the same build.
With --slug, v1's own film QA (overlay_clear_before_cuts) fails because the slug is on every frame. This is pre-existing v1 behaviour and left unchanged. v2's caption QA ignores the slug zone.
notes_for_builders: S04: the overlay chip reads per_frame.zoom from renders/meta/s04_subject.json; rerun make_overlays/assemble after any meta change. Please add a measured final s/f to the meta.

S05: render_finals calls `shots/s05_finale.py -- --mode final --frames <spec>` only after make_hex_tiles --require-final exits 0. qa_finals expects renders/<mode>/s05_finale/f_0001..0180.png. Title check pairs are v2 f121-180 with v1 s05_title f61-120.
Tiles: the frame count comes from meta `loop` (int; null/absent = 180). Frames are passed as dopa --frames specs such as 1-179:2 (interleaved chunks).
